source: JZ Mock A · Paper 1 · Question 9 · Publisher worked solution
knowledgePattern: Use circle centres and similar tangent triangles

hints.title: Read the two circles
hints.body: Complete squares to obtain both centres and radii, then calculate the distance between the centres.
hints.recap: A circle in completed-square form reveals its centre and squared radius.
hints.pitfall: The radius is the square root of the right-hand constant.
hints.pause: Mark these lengths on a sketch of the two circles and external tangents.

recall.reminder: A circle in completed-square form reveals its centre and squared radius.

hints.title: Add radii at the contacts
hints.body: Radii to a tangent are perpendicular. The centres lie along the angle bisector through the intersection of the tangents, giving similar right triangles.
hints.recap: Equal angle pairs establish similarity, so corresponding lengths have one common scale factor.
hints.pitfall: External tangents keep the centres on the same side; choose the order of the centres carefully.
hints.pause: Relate the two distances from P to the radius ratio and the centre separation.

recall.reminder: Equal angle pairs establish similarity, so corresponding lengths have one common scale factor.

solution:
1. Complete the squares: C1:x2+(y−4)2=80, C2:(x−3)2+y2=20. Thus A=(0,4), B=(3,0), with radii 45 and 25. Also AB=5.

2. Each centre is equidistant from the two tangent lines and lies on their angle bisector. As the circles lie on the same side of both external tangents, A, B and P lie on the same bisector ray, with the smaller circle nearer P.

3. Draw radii to one tangent. The two right triangles with vertex P are similar, so AP/BP=(45)/(25)=2. Since AP=AB+BP=5+BP, we obtain BP=5 and AP=10. Answer B.

4. Coordinate check: the line AB is y=4−4x/3. Its intersection with y=2x−16 is P=(6,−4), whose distance from A is 10.
